# Shortplay canvas baseline

This directory is the shared, replayable evidence set for the shortplay canvas
port. Files are split by provenance instead of presenting every sample as
production history.

## Evidence matrix

| Area | Files | Evidence | What it proves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Donor submap | `donor/` | runtime | Fixed donor `13731aae6` creates the six-child storyboard, edits the prompt and start-frame field, duplicates the subtree, persists, and reopens through a fresh repository |
| 4AI legacy rows | `legacy/payload-with-extensions.json` | runtime round-trip through the target SQLite repository | `row:<id>`, `batch-text:<id>`, row output bindings, batch cell overrides, resource owners and unknown extension fields survive |
| 4AI legacy resources | `legacy/resources.json` | schema sample | Resource ownership and asset payloads used by the legacy document |
| ZIP v3/v4 | `zip/projects-v3.json`, `zip/projects-v4.json` | reconstructed | Historical manifest identities, drawing document versions and archive paths |
| ZIP media entries | `zip/archive-entries.json` | reconstructed | Deterministic one-pixel media entries for read/import-path tests |
| Go/Web relation projection | `relation-projection.json` | shared semantic fixture | Field-to-edge order, R1-versus-frame overlap, text-reference order, copied-submap scope and deterministic edge IDs |

The donor capture is generated by:

```powershell
python scripts/shortplay-port/capture_donor_baseline.py `
  --donor-root "$env:TEMP\shortplay-donor-13731aae" `
  --out testdata/shortplay-canvas-port/donor
```

The donor worktree must be clean and at
`13731aae6c4cefadc2a1719e3e7e59b22e249f94`. The collector injects one temporary
test into the donor's `backend/internal/app` package and removes it afterwards.

## Runtime versus inference

- `donor/operations.json` is runtime evidence. It contains the command sequence,
  before/after snapshots, revision transitions, node order, reference order,
  projected edges, registered capability inventory and the field listing. Dynamic
  timestamp-valued fields are normalized; IDs, array order and scope IDs are not.
- `legacy/payload-with-extensions.json` is a schema-faithful reconstruction, not
  a production archive. The Go test writes it through
  `repository.UpsertCanvasProject` into an isolated SQLite database and reads the
  stored `PayloadJSON` back. This is a runtime persistence check for a
  reconstructed sample.
- `zip/*` is reconstructed from the exporter history. No historical ZIP was
  available locally, so it must not be described as production data.

## Replay commands

From `backend/`:

```powershell
go test -count=1 -run 'TestShortplayS01' -v ./internal/canvas
```

From `web/`:

```powershell
bun test test/shortplay-canvas-baseline.test.ts
bun test test/shortplay-relation-projection.test.ts
```

The relation fixture is consumed directly by both:

```powershell
go test -count=1 ./internal/canvas/relation
```

and the Web test above. A change to either projector must keep the same fixture
green in both runtimes.

The optional 200-node timing probe is intentionally opt-in:

```powershell
$env:SHORTPLAY_S01_MEASURE = "1"
go test -count=1 -run '^TestShortplayS01TargetTiming$' -v ./internal/canvas
```

On this machine, 10 rounds over a 200-node, 79,382-byte document produced
`open_avg=209.35µs` and `save_avg=3.05581ms` (SQLite, isolated temporary
database, local Windows host). These are local observations, not an SLA.

## Known baseline failures

The pinned donor also has pre-existing `document` round-trip failures for
`audio`, `image` and `video` render/parse fixtures (`logical:样例文本` is read
where `样例文本` is expected). They are recorded as donor baseline failures, not
as regressions caused by this port. The donor capture uses the isolated app
test helper, whose missing `shortplay_episodes` warning is likewise a local
fixture-table warning.
